meta.pageTitle: Claiming Asylum in Canada — Timeline | MC Guidance
meta.pageDescription: A general timeline to guide a person who is thinking about claiming asylum in Canada: 11 steps, from first reflection to settling in.

servicesPage.title: A general timeline to guide a person who is thinking about claiming asylum in Canada
servicesPage.intro: An 11-step journey, from the first reflection to settling in Canada. Find the step you are at today to receive general guidance adapted to your situation.
servicesPage.centralQuestion: What step are you at today?
servicesPage.centralQuestionNote: From there, we can place you in the right part of the timeline and give you general guidance adapted to your step.

steps.title: Reflection / general information
steps.description: The person begins to gather information. They want to understand whether Canada is an option, what claiming asylum means, what the risks are, which documents to prepare, and when they should speak to a lawyer or an authorized representative.
questions: What should my first reflex be?
Where are you right now, and what are you trying to understand first?
tips: Start looking for information from a consultant, on Google, or through someone you know.

steps.title: Preparing before departure
steps.description: The person has not yet started the journey or has not yet arrived in Canada. They want to prepare their story, their documents, their evidence, their identity papers, their children's or family's documents, and understand the main stages of the process.
questions: Do you already have your documents, your personal story, your important dates and your evidence organized?
How do you prepare before taking the road?
What is the best way to prepare before your departure?

steps.title: Travelling / arrival approaching
steps.description: The person is already on the move or close to arriving in Canada. At this step, the most important thing is to understand their overall situation: where they are, whether they are travelling alone or with family, whether they have documents, whether they are safe, and whether they need urgent help.
questions: Are you still on your way, already in Canada, or close to an official port of entry?

faq.q: While on the road, can you sense it coming?
faq.a: Yes. That was my case at the Boston airport in September 2017.

steps.title: Arrival in Canada / port of entry
steps.description: The person arrives in Canada through an airport, a land border crossing, or a seaport. They may be in contact with border officers. At this step, great caution is needed: guidance must remain general, and legal questions must be directed to a lawyer or an authorized representative.
questions: Have you already spoken with a Canadian immigration or border officer?
tips: Be vigilant and wise: tell the truth.

steps.title: Already in Canada, but no claim yet
steps.description: The person is already physically in Canada but has not yet started their asylum claim. They need to understand how to officially start their claim, which documents they must have, and how to organize their file.
questions: Have you already started an official claim, or are you still before that step?

faq.q: Is it possible to find a good lawyer or consultant to officially start your asylum claim without any referral?
faq.a: Yes — the Canadian government has set up social-service agencies to support you.

steps.title: Asylum claim started
steps.description: The person has already started their claim. They may have received instructions, a file number, an appointment, or a request for documents. At this step, we need to identify exactly what they have received and what is being asked next.
questions: What documents or instructions have you received from the Canadian authorities?

steps.title: Eligibility review
steps.description: IRCC or the CBSA reviews whether the claim can be sent to the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada. If the claim is eligible, it is referred to the IRB for the next part of the process.
questions: Have you been told whether your claim is eligible, or whether it has been referred to the IRB?

steps.title: Preparing the refugee file
steps.description: The person must organize their story, their dates, the important events, the threats or dangers they experienced, the evidence, the witnesses, medical documents, police reports, messages, photos, articles, or any other element that supports their account.
questions: Is your story clear, chronological, and supported by evidence where possible?
How do you prepare your story? What are the requirements?

steps.title: Preparing for the hearing
steps.description: The person is waiting for or preparing their hearing before the IRB. They need to understand the purpose of the hearing, review their story, check for possible inconsistencies, prepare their evidence, and work with a lawyer or an authorized representative if possible.
questions: Have you already received a hearing date, or are you still waiting?
How will you prepare for the hearing before meeting your lawyer?

steps.title: Decision
steps.description: After the hearing or the review of the file, the person receives a decision. If the decision is positive, they become a protected person. If the decision is negative, there may be very short deadlines to appeal or to seek another form of recourse.
questions: Have you received a decision? If so, is it positive or negative?
If the decision is favourable or unfavourable, what should you do?

steps.title: After the decision / settling in
steps.description: If the claim is accepted, the person needs to understand the next steps: protected person status, permanent residence, work, school, health care, housing, social assistance, integration, and community support.
questions: Do you need help with settling in, documents, work, school, health care or housing?

summary: I am preparing my documents and my story.
I am on my way or close to arriving.
I have arrived in Canada or at a port of entry.
I am already in Canada, but I have not applied yet.
I am waiting for the eligibility decision.
I am preparing my file and my evidence.
I am preparing for my hearing.
I am taking the steps after the decision and settling in.

footer.disclaimer: This information is general and does not constitute legal advice. For any legal question, consult a lawyer or an authorized representative.
